papers.title: Continuous generation of short-lived resident effector CD8 T cells sustains alopecia areata
papers.authors: Lee, Y.; Choi, J.; Lee, M.-s.; Kim, S.; Kang, J. J.; Shin, S.; Kim, T. H.; Ji, S. H.; Park, S.; Joo, S.; Lee, K.; Lee, C.; Lee, H.; Im, S. J.; Kwon, O.; Lee, J.-Y.; Lee, Y. J.
papers.abstract: CD8 T cells mediating chronic tissue inflammation have been thought to depend on stem-like progenitors that self-renew and replenish cytotoxic effector cells or exhausted progeny. Here, we show that stem-independent, short-lived resident effector CD8 T (TRE) cells sustain alopecia areata (AA), a common autoimmune disease that destroys hair follicles. AA-TRE cells exhibit TCR-dependent cytotoxicity, undergo rapid apoptosis in the skin, and lack memory or stem-like properties. Following adoptive transfer, donor TRE cells serve only as an initial trigger, whereas the host-derived CD103CD101 pathogenic pool is rebuilt continuously in skin-draining lymph nodes (sdLNs). Single-cell multiome and CUT&Tag profiling revealed that AA-TRE cells epigenetically silence Tox and upregulate RUNX2 to initiate the TRE differentiation program in sdLNs, while RUNX3 and AP-1s sustain it in the skin. Notably, CD8 T cells from patients with AA share this conserved regulatory network. Altogether, these findings define a distinct CD8 T cell differentiation state, offering new therapeutic implications for autoimmune diseases.

papers.title: Deep single-cell immune- and signaling profiles predict therapy response in chronic myeloid leukemia within hours.
papers.authors: Gullaksen SE, Brevik M, Craig E, Hellesøy M, Sefland Ø, Olsson-Strömberg U, Stentoft J, Richter J, Gedde-Dahl T, Tibshirani R, Plevritis SK, Wolf D, Mustjoki S, Hjorth-Hansen H, Gjertsen BT.
papers.abstract: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is effectively treated with small molecule BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) but as in all cancers, early identification of suboptimal responders and non-responders is a challenge. Through mass cytometry analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes collected on the first day of TKI treatment, we generated high-dimensional single-cell data from de novo chronic phase CML patients enrolled in two multicenter clinical trials (clinicaltrials.gov: NCT01725204 and NCT01061177). In leukocytes, dasatinib and nilotinib inhibited intracellular signaling within 1 or 3 h after first oral dose, respectively, and each TKI had a unique signaling signature reflecting its kinase specificity profile beyond BCR::ABL1. From these data, an immune and signaling profile was constructed for each patient that predicted the treatment response (BCR::ABL1 IS , %) during the first 12 months of treatment. The predictive features were drug specific: response to dasatinib was dominated by leukemic burden, neutrophil maturity (pSTAT3 Y705) and immune effector activity (pERK ½ in T- and NK cells), whereas response to nilotinib was driven by the intrinsic signaling states of CD34 + CD38 low CD25 + LSC-like cells (cleaved caspase-3, pCRKL Y207 and STAT3 [total and Y705]). These results show that single cell immune and signaling profiles measured within hours of first dose can predict 12-month treatment response, anticipating future optimization of kinase inhibitor treatment within days rather than months.

papers.title: Elflow: Automated Quality Control and Self-Supervised Representation Learning for High-Dimensional Cytometry
papers.authors: Kalakoti, Y.; Gasparetto, M.; Gupta, S. K.; Mittal, V.; Jha, A.
papers.abstract: High-dimensional flow and mass cytometry are foundational technologies for clinical immunophenotyping and hematological diagnostics, yet computational data analysis remains bottlenecked by operator-subjective manual gating. While computational tools have emerged, they remain fragmented across isolated tasks such as quality control or discrete clustering, leaving an unmet need for integrated, modular workflows that resolve continuous biological variation without manual supervision. Here, we introduce Elflow, a modular, self-supervised framework that links automated quality control, single-cell representation learning, and patient-level modeling without manual gating at inference. Elflow couples automated machine-learning quality control with Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization (VICReg) to learn continuous, batch-resilient single-cell representations without negative pairs or hand-labeled training sets. Across four diverse public benchmarks, Elflow adapts to distinct biological panels and clinical objectives. On 22-channel spectral flow cytometry (OMIP-030), self-supervised embeddings preserve fine functional T-cell gradations and outperform classical baselines in unsupervised clustering, while an anchor-guided extension accurately reproduces canonical manual gating hierarchies. On hand-curated CyTOF panels (Levine-13), linear PCA matches deep models, establishing an empirical boundary condition where linear methods suffice. Across multi-center clinical cohorts (FlowCAP-II), Elflow representations achieve high diagnostic sensitivity for acute myeloid leukemia across heterogeneous instruments despite severe class imbalance. In longitudinal immune monitoring (FlowCAP-IV), patient mean embeddings and micro-cluster differential histograms preserve rare antigen-specific responses, yielding significant AIDS-free survival stratification. By uniting automated quality control, self-supervised representation learning, and multi-scale patient aggregation, Elflow provides a modular, reproducibly benchmarked framework for high-parameter and multi-center translational cytometry.

papers.title: EOMES high PD-1 high CD103 + effector memory CD8 T cells in malignant pleural effusion: a distinct subset implicated in anti-tumor immunity and immunotherapeutic response.
papers.authors: Kim DK, Han HS, Sun P, Kim N, Lee D, Lee SI, Chung C, Lee JE, Park JO, Shin EC, Kang DH.
papers.abstract: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a frequent complication of advanced cancers and is associated with poor prognosis, including in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). We characterized T-cell populations in pleural effusion samples from patients with malignant ( n = 34) and benign ( n = 11) conditions using multiparametric flow cytometry and cytokine analysis, complemented by reanalysis of publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing datasets. MPE was characterized by enrichment of CD8⁺ effector memory (EM) T cells, including a distinct EOMES high PD-1 high CD103 + population. This subset exhibited increased expression of tissue residency-associated markers, including CD69 and CXCR6, together with increased granzyme B and Ki-67 expression and enhanced IFN- γ production following CD3/CD28 stimulation. Despite high PD-1 expression, it did not exhibit a coordinated increase in exhaustion-associated markers. Single-cell transcriptomic analyzes of breast cancer- and lung adenocarcinoma-associated MPE datasets identified related HLA-II⁺ CD8⁺ T-cell states with effector-associated features, and increased HLA-DR protein expression was confirmed by flow cytometry. Among patients receiving ICIs, this population was more abundant in those showing improvement in malignant pleural effusion, whose overall responses ranged from stable disease to partial response, whereas patients without pleural effusion improvement had progressive disease. These findings identify a tissue residency-associated, HLA-II-expressing CD8⁺ EM T-cell population with effector-associated features in MPE and suggest its potential clinical relevance during ICI therapy.

papers.title: Systematic Characterization of Clinically Actionable Antibody-Drug Targets Across Solid Tumors to Advance Precision Oncology.
papers.authors: Hu Z, Sun Y, Yuan J, Su T, Wang Y, Huang J, Taranto E, Jiang J, Nie J, Long M, Zhang JQ, Tanyi JL, Fan Y, Amaravadi RK, Kaufman J, Sommer J, Burr NS, Freed DM, Yang E, Cabanski CR, Li H, Montone KT, Kim SH, DeMichele A, Domchek SM, Hu X, Vonderheide RH, Zhang L.
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of antibody therapeutics is shifting the clinical bottleneck from drug availability to precise patient selection. We systematically characterize 87 clinically actionable tumor-associated antigens across solid tumors by integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, spatial, and single-cell profiles from more than 32,000 specimens to define expression prevalence, intratumoral heterogeneity, immune contexture, internalization and payload-sensitivity pathways, and translational relevance. We establish ANCHOR, a coordinate reference framework for standardizing patient RNA-seq data, and develop ReSort, a two-tiered scoring system for scalable target prioritization. ReSort enables virtual basket and umbrella trial matching, demonstrates concordance with clinical assays, predicts therapeutic response in patient-derived models, and identifies repurposing opportunities in rare malignancies. We develop an AI-based decision-support agent for antibody trial matching and construct a multimodal feature space integrating tumor- and protein-intrinsic attributes to guide systematic target discovery and prioritization. This work provides a scalable, clinically actionable approach for precision antibody-based therapies and next-generation target development.

papers.title: Spatial atlas of gut-draining lymph nodes reveals the developmental organization of intestinal tolerance and immunity
papers.authors: Lo, Y.; Lakhiani, P.; Yadav, A.; Feather, G.; C. Binoy, A.; Paucar Iza, Y. A.; Parisotto, Y.; Hoelting, T.; Shibu, G.; Cabric, V.; Park, T.; Brown, C.
papers.abstract: Early life offers a window to establish lasting tolerance to dietary and commensal microbial antigens. How developing gut lymph nodes balance tolerance and immunity remains unclear. Using spatial transcriptomics, we map small intestine- and colon-draining nodes during weaning and adulthood, resolving rare immune and stromal populations and their niches, including Thetis cells (TCs), an antigen-presenting lineage critical for intestinal tolerance. We uncover a peri-weaning subcapsular compartment enriched for TC I but depleted of classical antigen-relaying macrophages, coincident with attenuated follicular responses. Peri-weaning colonic nodes are hubs of T cell activation enriched for peripherally-induced regulatory T (pTreg) cell responses. We resolve distinct classical dendritic cell (cDC) and TC niches, including a pTreg-associated niche shared by TC IV and CCR7 cDC2. We further characterize a distinct population of intestinal tissue TCs, and establish TC migration to draining lymph nodes. Together, our atlas provides a framework for understanding how the timing of intestinal antigen exposure intersects with developing lymph node niches to shape tolerance or immunity.

papers.title: CIRCA learns identifiable cell- and niche-level programs and their interactions with tissue pathology from spatial transcriptomics
papers.authors: Lovelace, T. C.; Tung, C.-H.; Enduru, N.; Zhao, Z.
papers.abstract: Interactions among cells and their local microenvironments shape tissue organization and function, while their dysregulation can contribute to disease. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), the complex responses of glial cells and neurons to amyloid-{beta} pathology can both mitigate and exacerbate neuronal injury. Spatial transcriptomics enables investigation of these relationships in situ, but recovering interpretable transcriptional programs and their interactions from spatial transcriptomics remains challenging, in part because conventional nonlinear models are non-identifiable. Here we present CIRCA (Causal Interaction Representation for Cellular Architectures), a self-supervised causal representation learning framework that jointly learns identifiable cell- and neighborhood-level transcriptional programs and the directed interactions among them under explicit assumptions. It can also be extended to incorporate additional modalities such as pathology. Benchmarked against five existing methods across seven cell-resolution datasets, CIRCA achieved the highest biological accuracy in six and the highest overall score in all five multi-section datasets, while recovering higher-order anatomical organization. In an AD mouse model, incorporating amyloid-{beta} pathology revealed four region-specific plaque niches enriched for microglia. Plaque-associated microglia shared a core disease-associated response whose strength varied by region, and AD genetic risk was preferentially enriched in hippocampal and cortical plaque-associated microglia. Reproducible latent factors linked to cell-level amyloid burden separated phagocytic from inflammatory microglial programs. Applied to a human colorectal cancer dataset, CIRCA resolved patient-specific tumor niches, conserved stromal remodeling niches, and distinct macrophage states, highlighting its versatility. Together, these results establish CIRCA as a methodological advance over existing approaches, enabling deeper insights into tissue organization and the molecular dependencies linking cells to their local environments.

papers.title: Functional and lncRNA changes in ovine blood monocytes and derived macrophages following paratuberculosis vaccination.
papers.authors: Mendívil P, Arteche-Villasol N, Elguezabal N, Mugica-Unamuno M, Molina E, Fernández I, Criado M, Silva M, Gutiérrez-Expósito D, Benavides J, Fernández M.
papers.abstract: Vaccination is central to control paratuberculosis in ruminants. Commercial vaccines such as Gudair ® , although not fully preventing infection, reduce clinical signs and faecal shedding. Nevertheless, their protective immunological mechanisms remain unclear. This study evaluated the effect of Gudair ® vaccination on mononuclear phagocyte function in sheep (Ovis aries) and correlated it with their long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) expression. Ten Assaf lambs were divided into vaccinated (n = 5) and non-vaccinated (n = 5) groups. Peripheral blood was collected before vaccination and at 30-, 60- and 90-days post-vaccination (dpv) to assess antigen-specific IFN-γ and antibody responses. Phagocytosis and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production were evaluated in the monocyte fraction following in vitro Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (Map) infection of whole blood. At 90 dpv, monocytes were also isolated from peripheral blood to generate ovine monocyte-derived macrophages (OvMDMs) to assess Map phagocytosis and intracellular survival and lncRNAs expression analysis by RNA-seq. Vaccination induced increased IFN-γ and anti-Map antibody responses over time. Monocytes from vaccinated lambs showed significantly higher ROS production at 90 dpv (p < 0.05), whereas phagocytosis did not differ between groups. No significant differences were observed in OvMDMs regarding Map phagocytosis or bacterial survival. Transcriptome analysis of monocytes at 90 dpv identified 6854 lncRNAs (4719 annotated and 2135 novel), of which four were differentially expressed between groups. Cis- and trans-based computational analyses identified potential associations with genes involved in immune-related pathways. These findings improve our understanding of the innate immune responses induced by paratuberculosis vaccination and identify candidate lncRNAs for further investigation in vaccine-induced immunity.

papers.title: Drastic improvement in MHC class I epitope prediction through training data augmentation, generative adversarial network modeling of selfness, and consideration of homology to class II epitopes.
papers.authors: Oh, S.; Hong, S.-E.; Kim, H.-S.; Paik, S.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of immunogenic neoantigens is critical for personalized cancer vaccines but remains hindered by the high false-positive rates of current predictors. Here, we present DeepOmicsNeo, a modular deep learning framework that harmonizes three biological determinants of immunogenicity. The first module, DeepOmicsNeo-Binding, overcomes data scarcity in non-9mer peptide-Class I Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) binding prediction via a novel augmentation strategy that synthesizes pseudo-binders and non-binders by editing non-anchor residues, outperforming its competitors. The second module, DeepOmicsNeo-Selfness, addresses the paucity of negative training data for immunogenicity prediction by utilizing a Generative Adversarial Network trained on around 60 million human self-peptides. This unsupervised approach quantifies selfness to detect immunogenic peptides and the resulting score correlated with IFN-{gamma} secretion by T-cells. The third module, DeepOmicsNeo-H2, exploits the central-region homology between known HLA Class-I and Class-II restricted epitopes. The integrated model, DeepOmicsNeo-Immunogenicity, outperforms state-of-the-art predictors on the TESLA, HiTIDE, and TiTANIAN benchmark datasets.[2.1] Top20 precision, the most important benchmark for clinical utility in personalized cancer vaccine design, was drastically improved over other predictors. Together, these findings indicate that jointly modeling the three complementary features captures biologically meaningful determinants of immunogenicity, supporting DeepOmicsNeo as a robust computational framework for neoantigen prioritization in personalized cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Measuring the information budget of cross-target antibody affinity generalization: a robust cross-target wall, and why structure reaches developability but not affinity
papers.authors: de Melo Martins, L.; Zenatti Salles, P. P.; Meidanis, J.
papers.abstract: Structure-based machine learning is widely expected to advance antibody engineering, yet it is unclear how far affinity predictions transfer to new targets, and why. We introduce a noise-corrected, censoring-aware estimator of the cross-target transfer ceiling, {rho}max = {surd}(T/(T+I)), which separates a transferable antibody-intrinsic component (T) from a non-transferable target-specific interaction (I). On deterministic synthetic ground truth the estimator recovers the noise-free ceiling to {+/-} 0.0003, whereas the naive sum-of-squares estimator is biased downward by measurement noise. Applying it from synthetic to real systems, the transferable budget is small, and on real neutralization panels it is not an artefact: the target-specific interaction survives noise and censoring correction. It is strongly regime-dependent, with a two-tier structure: predicting a novel antibody from sequence alone (the design setting) reaches a lower ceiling ({rho} {approx} 0.44 on real breadth data) than ranking a characterized one ({rho} {approx} 0.59), even with a strong protein language model. Synthetic oracles also overstate transferability: an oracle scored on real predicted structures carries about half the budget of a matched synthetic lattice (0.45 vs. 0.81), and real neutralization and escape panels sit well below the synthetic ceiling (0.32-0.68). Under leakage-free antigen-cluster splits, cross-target affinity ranking across every method family collapses to this budget, while within a sampled target a structure-based graph network ranks affinity above off-the-shelf FoldX and GearBind (within-complex Spearman 0.55), and structural surface descriptors predict a surface-driven developability property (hydrophobic aggregation) where sequence-dominated properties (humanness, charge-driven self-association) do not benefit. A controlled ablation attributes the residual within-target signal to the antibody alone: dropping the antigen from the structural model leaves it essentially unchanged (interface {Delta} {rho} between -0.01 and +0.02 across four panels), so for this model the paratope-epitope interface adds no ranking signal over the antibody alone. Models climb toward the budget within a target -- via a measure-then-rank operating mode that recovers top binders 6-8 times more efficiently than random once a target has been sampled -- but none crosses it.

papers.title: Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Huang Y, Sun W, Zhang H, Matsui M.
papers.abstract: Plateau aquatic environments expose fishes to chronic cold, hypoxia, ultraviolet radiation and low productivity, providing natural systems for studying genomic features associated with environmental adaptation. Whether related fishes inhabiting similar cold-water plateau environments exhibit comparable or divergent genomic responses remains unclear. We compared two plateau cypriniform fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus , within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, chromosome-scale synteny and duplicated gene-pair divergence profiling. The strongest contrasts occurred in species-specific orthogroups and gene-family turnover. Aspiorhynchus laticeps had a larger set of apparent species-specific orthogroups, enriched mainly in oocyte and reproductive processes, and its expanded families and elevated- ω orthogroups were associated with immune, receptor-mediated and membrane-associated functions. By contrast, D. maculatus had fewer species-specific orthogroups enriched for neural and synaptic processes and a contraction-dominated gene-family profile involving host defence, mucosal immunity and chromatin-related processes. The focal contrast did not exceed empirical background variation, and expansion-related computational analysis of gene family evolution (CAFE) estimates were associated with assembly continuity and input-gene properties. These findings indicate that ecologically similar plateau fishes may exhibit different combinations of candidate genomic features, highlighting the joint influence of ecological adaptation and genome history.

papers.title: A functional TIGIT-associated transcriptional program identifies circulating tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells in melanoma patients.
papers.authors: Zhao F, Hua Y, Ghorbani F, Kwapik S, Brüggemann A, Kelly K, Majewski E, Möller I, Zaremba A, Roesch A, Lennerz V, Hennig S, Heinold A, Kropp KN, Llamazares-Prada M, Plass C, Schadendorf D, Sucker A, Rambow F, Paschen A.
papers.abstract: Accessing tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells in patient blood is essential for non-invasive monitoring of systemic T cell responses and guiding personalized therapies. However, precise functional, molecular, and phenotypic characterization of these cells remains challenging. Here, we identify TIGIT as a functionally validated surrogate marker of tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells and define its associated transcriptional program to characterize circulating tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells in melanoma patients. We demonstrate that blood TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cells mount robust cytotoxic responses against autologous tumor cells across multiple melanoma patient models, irrespective of PD-1 co-expression. At the clonotype level, TIGIT broadened detection of the circulating tumor-reactive repertoire beyond PD-1 while retaining high specificity. Moreover, circulating TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cell population was closely associated with the intratumoral T cell repertoire and exhibited hallmarks of antigen experience, including effector memory differentiation, a hypomethylated DNA landscape, and increased clonal expansion. Longitudinal profiling of blood samples from melanoma patients undergoing immune checkpoint inhibition revealed an increased frequency of TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cells in clinical responders. Finally, leveraging paired single-cell transcriptomic and TCR data from patient models with identified tumor-reactive clones, we show that the TIGIT-associated transcriptional program enables robust detection of circulating tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells. Collectively, our data establish TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cells as a potent reservoir of tumor-reactive T cells in peripheral blood and provide a blood-based framework for accelerating TCR discovery and advancing adoptive cell therapy.

papers.title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab in surgically resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (PRIME-HCC): a prospective, phase 1b, single-arm trial and translational analyses.
papers.authors: D'Alessio A, Fulgenzi CAM, Pai M, Schlaak AE, Spalding D, Godbole I, Goldin RD, Acuti N, Ward C, Nteliopoulos G, Yip V, Slater S, Rajagopal P, Sodergren M, Tait P, Habib N, Thomas R, Maher E, Mauri FA, Cortellini A, Marchesi JR, Bengsch B, Sharma R, Pinato DJ.
papers.abstract: Background Nivolumab plus ipilimumab improves survival in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. We evaluated this combination as neoadjuvant therapy and investigated its effect on peripheral immunity and the tumour microenvironment. Methods PRIME-HCC is a single-arm, phase 1b trial in adults (aged ≥18 years) with early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, Child-Pugh A liver function, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1. Patients received nivolumab (3 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 22 of the first and second cycle) and ipilimumab (1 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 of the first cycle only) before liver resection. The primary endpoint was safety, assessed by treatment-related delays to surgery and adverse events in the intention-to-treat population. Translational analyses included imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on paired tumour samples, peripheral immunophenotyping, T-cell receptor (TCR) β sequencing, and longitudinal tumour-agnostic circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) profiling. This trial was registered with EudraCT (2018-000987-27) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03682276); follow-up is currently ongoing. Findings Between Sept 18, 2019, and Sept 28, 2023, of 43 patients assessed for eligibility, 33 patients were enrolled (25 [76%] male and 8 [24%] female; median age 68 years [range 38-80; IQR 63-73]); median follow-up was 25·7 months (95% CI 21·2-30·1). Any-grade adverse events occurred in 31 (94%) of patients, with treatment-related adverse events (trAEs) in 25 (76%) patients. Grade 3 trAEs occurred in three (9%) patients (transaminase elevation, anaemia, and dyspnoea). Serious adverse events were recorded in three (9%) patients, and no grade 4-5 events or treatment-related deaths occurred. 30 (91%) patients underwent surgery, including two (6%) who had immune checkpoint inhibitor-related surgical delays. Objective response rate by RECIST 1.1 was noted in eight (25%; 95% CI 13-42) patients (one complete response and seven partial responses), with 31 (97%; 84-100) patients achieving disease control. The absence of ctDNA after surgery was associated with improved 2-year recurrence-free survival (nine [82%] of 11 patients vs two [29%] of seven; p=0·049), as was at least 50% ctDNA reduction (median not reached [95% CI not reached] vs 20·9 months [95% CI 16·3-25·4]; HR 0·14 [95% CI 0·02-0·91]; p=0·039). Patients with objective responses showed expansion of peripheral PD-1-positive, Ki-67-positive, CD8-positive T cells (T-responding exhausted cells [Tresp]), associated with higher baseline intratumoral progenitor-exhausted T cells (Tpex) and increased Tresp infiltration. Patients whose disease did not respond to treatment exhibited enrichment of terminally exhausted CD8-positive T cells (Tex-term; CD8-positive PD-1-positive TOX-positive cells) and regulatory T cells. Interpretation Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab is feasible in early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, and later-phase randomised trials are needed to confirm the efficacy of this treatment strategy. Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring could support detection of minimal residual disease and warrants further prospective validation. Funding Bristol Myers Squibb, Cancer Research UK, Associazione Italiana per la Ricerca sul Cancro, and Foundation for Liver Research.

papers.title: Comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing analysis reveals key immune regulators and signaling pathways in people living with HIV across tissues and cell types.
papers.authors: Nguyen HD, Siddiqui S, Kim WK.
papers.abstract: Objectives To identify shared gene signatures, regulatory networks, and shared molecular regulators associated with HIV infection across tissues and cell types using publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets from people living with HIV. Methods We systematically analyzed human scRNA-seq datasets from brain, cerebrospinal fluid, blood, adipose tissue, and peripheral immune cells from people living with HIV with or without antiretroviral therapy and uninfected controls. HIV-associated genes were identified across datasets, followed by network, transcription factor, and microRNA analyses to identify shared regulatory programs. Findings were evaluated in independent human datasets and validated by immunohistochemistry in brain tissue from simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV)-infected rhesus macaques. Results Nineteen HIV-associated genes were shared across sample types, including seven hub genes (CD68, TIMP1, AIF1, EGR1, IL1B, MS4A6A, and SPI1). These genes were enriched in immune activation, innate immune systems, and inflammatory pathways. Regulatory network analysis identified SPI1 as a highly connected transcriptional regulator and hsa-miR-155-5p as a prominent microRNA regulator. SPI1 and EGR1 showed increased detection in independent human HIV datasets and increased protein detection in SIV-infected macaque brain tissue. Conclusions Cross-dataset single-cell transcriptomic analysis identified HIV-associated molecular programs across biological compartments and highlighted SPI1 and EGR1 as candidates and potential regulators of HIV-associated inflammation. These findings provide a framework for further investigation of their roles in HIV-associated complications, including HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders and cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Durable CD8-mediated remission after brief anti-HIV-1 antibody treatment requires FcγR engagement.
papers.authors: Bournazos S, Nishimura Y, Grace BAC, Niejadlik EG, Rogan DC, Meeks T, Webber JD, Przygonska PA, Lehman H, Minster VE, Jesteadt E, Sadjadpour R, Connors M, Martin MA, Ravetch JV.
papers.abstract: Despite highly efficacious antiretroviral therapy (ART), durable ART-free remission remains a central objective of HIV-1 cure strategies. The randomized, placebo-controlled RIO trial recently demonstrated that long-acting broadly neutralizing anti-HIV-1 antibodies (bNAbs) can sustain prolonged virologic control after ART interruption, including control that persisted beyond the period of therapeutically relevant antibody concentrations, providing clinical evidence consistent with host-mediated suppression. However, the mechanisms underlying these "vaccinal" effects remain unresolved. Here, we establish Fcγ receptor (FcγR) engagement as an essential driver of multiyear remission after bNAb therapy in simian-human immunodeficiency virus (SHIV)-infected macaques. Brief therapy during acute infection with Fc domain variants of the bNAb 3BNC117, matched for antigen binding, neutralizing activity, and pharmacokinetics but differing in FcγR engagement, produced comparable early virologic control yet profoundly divergent long-term outcomes. Sustained CD8 T cell-dependent suppression lasting nearly 300 wk developed in every evaluable animal receiving the FcγR-engaging variant but arose in only one of eight recipients of the FcγR-null variant. FcγR-driven immunomodulation imprinted a CD8 T cell response characterized by enhanced antigen-specific effector function, early clonal focusing with sustained clonotype persistence, and distinct cellular-state transcriptional signatures. Our findings identify the Fc-FcγR axis as a critical determinant of the reliable induction of durable remission and provide a mechanistic framework for developing Fc-engineered bNAbs designed to enhance vaccinal immunity and advance antibody-based strategies with the potential to achieve functional cure.
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: Author Correction: A machine learning model reveals expansive downregulation of ligand-receptor interactions that enhance lymphocyte infiltration in melanoma with developed resistance to immune checkpoint blockade.
papers.authors: Sahni S, Wang B, Wu D, Dhruba SR, Nagy M, Patkar S, Ferreira I, Day CP, Wang K, Ruppin E.

papers.title: Unveiling MLLT3: A Key Transcription Factor in ESCC Prognosis and Immune Infiltration.
papers.authors: Li S, Zhang Y, Bai Y.
papers.abstract: The transcription factor Myeloid/lymphoid or mixed-lineage leukemia; translocated to, 3 (MLLT3) super elongation complex subunit plays an important role in the regulation of oncogenes and suppressor genes during cancer progression; however, how they participate in the occurrence and development of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) has yet to be fully elucidated. Using Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), differential expression analysis of 1,834 transcription factors (TFs) was performed, which identified 251 up-regulated and 159 down-regulated TFs. Enrichment analysis revealed that differentially expressed TFs (DETFs) were implicated in the transcriptional misregulation of cancer. A total of 17 candidate DETFs were associated with survival. Subsequently, transcription factor like 5 (TCFL5), MLLT3, zinc finger family (ZNF) 274, and ZNF 697 were identified as four key genes associated with disease progression by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator and random forest algorithms. In univariable Cox regression with hazard ratios expressed per 1 standard deviation (SD) of expression, MLLT3 [HR = 0.430, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.267-0.693, P = 5.2 × 10 -4 ; Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p = 0.009] was the transcription factor most strongly associated with overall survival. Single-cell transcriptome data showed that MLLT3 was exceptionally expressed in T cell subpopulations. Pan-cancer analysis revealed that MLLT3 exhibited significant positive correlations with CD4 + resting memory T cells across 14 cancer types. Notably, in esophageal carcinoma (ESCA), MLLT3 expression showed a moderately strong positive correlation with CD4 + resting memory T cell infiltration (Spearman rho = 0.452, P = 1.91 × 10 -10 ), suggesting a potential association. Reduced MLLT3 expression was detected in ESCC, suggesting its potential tumor-suppressor role. In vitro experiments demonstrated that MLLT3 knockdown significantly promoted cancer cell proliferation and migration. Mechanistically, MLLT3 may modulate the levels of phosphorylated extracellular signal-regulated kinase, a key effector in the mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling pathway, thereby mediating its anti-tumor effects. These findings indicate that MLLT3 acts as a tumor suppressor gene, providing novel insights into its dual role in shaping immune infiltration and disease progression.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Machine Learning for Prioritizing Candidate Plasma Proteins in Alzheimer's Disease and Predicting Multi-Target Interactions of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.authors: Lin H, Huang Z, Liao Z, Wu Q, Cui L.
papers.abstract: This study integrated multi-omics data and machine learning to prioritize candidate plasma proteins and to predict the multi-target interactions of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Mendelian randomization across three cohorts (Icelandic, UK Biobank, and Fenland) identified 66 AD-associated plasma proteins, including TREM2, ACE, GRN, and CR1, with TREM2 showing a robust protective effect (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.75-0.81). Single-cell RNA sequencing showed neuron-specific downregulation of NSF and TMEM106B in AD, implicating synaptic dysfunction and impaired axonal transport. A machine-learning classifier (K-nearest neighbors, KNN) incorporating TREM2, TMEM106B, C1S, PLOD2, and NSF, trained on brain-tissue expression data, demonstrated moderate predictive performance (AUC = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.63-0.90) and is presented as a candidate brain-tissue-derived classifier rather than a validated non-invasive plasma diagnostic panel. Immune infiltration analysis revealed altered M2 macrophage and plasma cell dynamics, with NSF negatively correlated with γδ T-cell infiltration (p < 0.001). Network pharmacology prioritized five candidate TCM herbs (e.g., Scutellaria baicalensis [Huang Qin] and Alpinia oxyphylla [Yi Zhi]) and bioactive compounds (stigmasterol and quercetin) targeting AD-related proteins. Molecular docking predicted strong binding between stigmasterol and PLOD2 (binding energy: -11.2kcal/mol), suggesting a potential role in modulating extracellular matrix remodeling. These compounds were enriched in the PI3K-Akt and NF-κB pathways, consistent with the anti-inflammatory effects observed in TCM formulations such as GHYSJ. These findings link candidate biomarker discovery with the predicted multi-target interactions of TCM, providing hypotheses for future non-invasive diagnosis and precision therapy in AD.

papers.title: Brain border-associated macrophages rhythmically scavenge amyloid-beta and regulate vascular amyloid pathology.
papers.authors: Barr HJ, Caldwell SK, Colville-Reimertz JM, Depp C, Walker AJ, Patel J, Marsh SE, Gupte AS, Hingerl M, Park SO, Ferraro S, Lipton J, Stevens B.
papers.abstract: Circadian disruptions perturb the brain and immune system and increase the risk of developing Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet whether this involves dysregulation of brain immunity remains less clear. Here, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of the brain immune compartment around the day-night cycle and identified brain border-associated macrophages (BAMs) as highly rhythmic cells. We found that the rest phase was a specialized time for BAM engulfment, characterized by upregulation of endocytic machinery and enhanced uptake of fluid-borne material including amyloid-beta (Aβ). Rhythmicity in BAM scavenging was regulated by the clock gene Bmal1, mediated by the scavenger receptor CD206, and perturbed with age. In a mouse model of AD, deletion of Bmal1 in BAMs worsened perivascular and leptomeningeal Aβ plaque burden. Our results characterize rapid endocytosis as a specialized and rhythmic BAM function and identify perturbed timing of brain border immunity as one avenue by which circadian disruptions may precipitate amyloidosis.

papers.title: TNF-α signaling is downregulated in CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, and monocytes in people with HIV with abnormal diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide.
papers.authors: Chung N, Dai G, Vance A, Branchini J, Zhang MH, Byanova KL, Smith DL, Shimoda M, Maliskova L, Eckalbar W, Hunt PW, Huang L, Lin J.
papers.abstract: Objective An abnormal diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLco) is the most prevalent lung function abnormality seen in people with HIV, but the drivers of this phenotype are poorly understood. We aimed to understand the molecular mechanisms underlying abnormal DLco in the context of chronic HIV infection, both in the local lung environment and in circulating peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Design A cross-sectional, observational, and transcriptomic pilot study. Methods We collected and isolated PBMCs from eight PWH and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) cells from 29 PWH enrolled in the I AM OLD-DA study in San Francisco, CA. We conducted single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) for PBMCs and bulk RNA-seq for BAL samples and performed downstream differential gene expression (DGE) and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). We used ATS/ERS-compliant pulmonary function tests (PFTs) to classify the participants' DLco as normal [DLco ≥ lower limit of normal (LLN)] or abnormal (DLco Results In PBMCs, we observed upregulation of interferon pathways in CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and downregulation of TNF-α signaling across CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, and monocytes in PWH with an abnormal DLco. Analysis of BAL revealed upregulation of PI3K-mTOR signaling, oxidative phosphorylation, and MYC target V1 pathways, which were not observed in major cell types from PBMCs. Conclusion Abnormal DLco in PWH was associated with a shared interferon-driven transcriptional signature and broad downregulation of TNF-α signaling across multiple immune cell subsets, along with distinct metabolic pathway enrichment in BAL, suggesting separate systemic and pulmonary immune mechanisms.

papers.title: Endothelial cells and interstitial macrophages determine tissue-specific responses to type I IFNs in mice expressing humanized IFNARs.
papers.authors: Yuan J, Li J, Zhang M, Feng C, Shi J, Wang Y, Jiang M, Fan Q, Wei Z, Wu Q, Zhang L, Li F.
papers.abstract: The human type I interferons (IFN-Is) IFN-α2 and IFN-β are used as immunoregulators to treat viral infections and multiple sclerosis, respectively. Their different binding affinities for the type I IFN receptor (IFNAR) determine their intracellular signal intensity in vitro. However, the species specificity of IFNs restricts the investigation of their functional differences in vivo. Here, we analyzed the induction of IFN-stimulated genes (ISGs) in response to exogenous low-dose administration of IFN-α2 and IFN-β in human THP-1 cells and in HuIFNAR mice, which express the humanized IFNAR subunits HuIFNAR1 and HuIFNAR2. In THP-1 cells, IFN-β stimulated a more rapid and robust early ISG response than did IFN-α2, but the response to IFN-α2 was more sustained. In the HuIFNAR mice, IFN-β and IFN-α2 induced tissue-specific profiles of ISGs. Among the 1752 ISGs induced by IFN-β or IFN-α2, only 81 ISGs were induced by both. In contrast with the observations in THP-1 cells, IFN-α2 induced a broader and more robust ISG response compared with that of IFN-β in multiple tissues. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that endothelial cells in the lung exhibited the highest expression of tissue-specific ISGs and were the primary cell type shaping the tissue-specific ISG landscape, whereas immune cells, particularly interstitial macrophages, drove IFN subtype-specific differences in ISG expression. Together, our findings uncover tissue- and cell type-specific functional differences between IFN-α2 and IFN-β, revealing that the in vivo activities of IFN-I subtypes are determined by both tissue context and cellular composition.

papers.title: Key molecules, diagnostic models and immune microenvironment analysis of ischemic stroke based on pyroptosis and immunosuppression-related genes.
papers.authors: Mou J, Liu H, Hong Y, Fang D, Ge X, Cai Q.
papers.abstract: Ischemic Stroke (IS) represents a significant global health challenge due to its high morbidity and mortality rates, necessitating an urgent need for enhanced diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. The present study aimed to construct a multi-gene diagnostic model for IS while elucidating the underlying molecular mechanisms and identifying critical genes associated with pyroptosis and immune suppression. Utilizing data from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) repositories, specifically datasets GSE16561 and GSE22255, we initially identified 5,992 nominally significant differentially expressed candidate genes that were subsequently cross-referenced with gene sets related to pyroptosis and immune suppression. Employing Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), we isolated pivotal genes within key modules, which, through rigorous cross-validation combined with protein-protein interaction networks and multiple machine learning algorithms, culminated in the identification of six core model genes: TNF, STAT3, MMP9, MYD88, TLR2, and JAK2. These genes demonstrated significant involvement in inflammatory responses, lipid metabolism, and Toll-like receptor signaling pathways, contributing to the construction of a diagnostic model. This model exhibited favorable discriminative performance in the training dataset; however, external evaluation in an independent cohort (GSE22255) with fixed model coefficients did not support its cross-cohort generalizability. Furthermore, consistency clustering revealed two distinct IS subtypes characterized by unique molecular profiles, while immune cell infiltration analysis highlighted notable alterations in the IS immune microenvironment. Collectively, our findings identify candidate biomarkers and two exploratory expression-based subtypes associated with IS, and reveal immune microenvironment alterations; these results are hypothesis-generating, and their diagnostic and therapeutic implications require functional and prospective clinical validation.

papers.title: Cancer vaccines in the era of immunotherapy: from antigen delivery to immune ecosystem engineering.
papers.authors: Mouren AP, Ott PA.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic cancer vaccines reliably induce tumour-specific immune responses, although translating this immunogenicity into durable tumour control remains a major challenge. This disconnect is probably the result of a series of biological bottlenecks, from antigen selection and presentation to T cell priming, tumour infiltration and resistance to immune suppression. Advances in neoantigen identification, vaccine technologies, immune profiling and computational biology have renewed and re-energized the field. Emerging evidence from clinical trials testing neoantigen-directed vaccines indicates that therapeutic vaccination can improve clinical outcomes particularly when applied in earlier disease settings and integrated within broader immunotherapeutic strategies. In this Review, we examine the mechanisms limiting vaccine efficacy, discuss how they are informing the design of next-generation vaccines, and explore the biomarkers and therapeutic strategies that might enable vaccination to achieve more consistent clinical benefit.

papers.title: Circulating TOX+ TIGIT+ CD57+ TEMRA CD8+ T cells are associated with efficacy of combined aPD-L1, aCTLA-4 and metronomic chemotherapy in advanced cervical cancer.
papers.authors: Bertucci A, Maby P, Chrétien AS, Granjeaud S, Reine C, Ben-Amara A, Rouvière MS, Gorvel L, Billon E, Chanez B, Legrand F, Cropet C, Frenel JS, Le Tourneau C, Hervieu A, Coquan E, de La Motte Rouge T, Saada-Bouzid E, Lavaud P, Hédou J, Gaudillière B, Lisberg A, Sabatier R, Gonçalves A, Olive D, Rochigneux P.
papers.abstract: To improve ICI efficacy in advanced CC, a promising strategy is to combine anti-PDL-1, anti-CTLA-4 and chemotherapy. The phase I/II MOVIE trial reported a clinical benefit rate of 53.1% of durvalumab, tremelimumab and metronomic oral vinorelbine in patients with pretreated metastatic CC. The objective of this study is to discover immune efficacy biomarkers of this combination. We analyzed 29 advanced CC patients from MOVIE multicentric prospective clinical trial (NCT03518606). We used high-dimensional mass cytometry (CyTOF) to explore the immune landscape in baseline peripheral blood mononuclear cells. We developed 3 immune panels of 40 antibodies (T cells, NK cells and myeloid cells) for the deep-phenotyping of PBMCs. Our bioinformatics workflow of CyTOF data included dimensionality reduction (opt-SNE, UMAP), automated clustering (PhenoGraph) and regression (CITRUS). The biomarker candidates were submitted to a model prediction composed of 11 machine-learning algorithms. In baseline blood samples, high-dimensional analyses consistently identified a population of TOX+TIGIT+CD57+ TEMRA (CD45RA+CCR7-) CD8+ T cells associated with improved clinical outcomes: clinical benefit (CB), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). This population was confirmed by manual gating and 11 machine-learning algorithms. After determining a cut-off at 0.73% of CD45+ cells, patients with an increased blood baseline frequency of TOX+TIGIT+CD57+ TEMRA (CD45RA+CCR7-) CD8+ T cells had an improved CBR (76% vs 25%, p=0.005), an improved PFS (HR=0.35, CI95, 0.13-0.95, p=0.013) and an improved OS (HR=0.19, CI95, 0.07-0.53, p=0.001). Multivariate analysis with classical CC prognostic factors confirmed the OS benefit of our biomarker (HR=0.15, CI95: 0.05-0.47, <0.001).

papers.title: CyFj11: FlowJo v11 Workspace Import and Legacy Format Export for R-Based Flow Cytometry Analysis.
papers.authors: Jagla B, Culina S, Le Guerroue F, Karkeni E, Hasan M.
papers.abstract: High-dimensional flow cytometry measures immune cells at single-cell resolution, enabling systematic characterization of cell populations at scale. But harnessing this potential requires seamless interoperability between the interactive gating tools used by biologists and the statistical environments used for detailed downstream analysis. FlowJo, one of the most widely used commercial cytometry analysis software packages, now stores workspaces in a format that existing R tools cannot read, leaving researchers unable to import their gating strategies into R or to return R-based results to FlowJo for visual review or collaborative sharing without manual reconstruction. We present CyFj11, an R package that closes this gap, enabling import of FlowJo v11 gating hierarchies into R and export of R-defined gates back to FlowJo (throughout this paper, "import" refers to bringing a FlowJo v11 workspace into R, and "export" to writing an R-derived GatingSet back out to FlowJo). Using a combination of synthetic test scenarios and a real-world immunophenotyping dataset, we show that population counts in FlowJo 10 and 11 matched R-derived values with Pearson correlation coefficients exceeding 0.99. CyFj11 is platform-independent, requires no additional software infrastructure, and is freely available at https://github.com/C3BI-pasteur-fr/CyFj11.
papers.venue: Cytometry. Part A : the journal of the International Society for Analytical Cytology

papers.title: Precision immunopharmacology in xenotransplantation: integrating genome-engineered donors, organoid testbeds, and AI-guided translation.
papers.authors: Ren T, Fu G, Duan S, Zeng M, Gao Y.
papers.abstract: Xenotransplantation is moving from isolated proof-of-concept procedures toward an engineered biotechnology platform for organ replacement. This review examines how genome-designed donor pigs, recipient-directed immunopharmacology, human-relevant in vitro testbeds, and data-driven decision systems can be integrated to address the remaining barriers to clinical translation. CRISPR-Cas-based engineering enables deletion of dominant carbohydrate xenoantigens, insertion of human complement- and coagulation-regulatory genes, modulation of innate and adaptive immune checkpoints, control of donor-organ growth, and inactivation of porcine endogenous retrovirus sequences. However, donor engineering does not eliminate residual T-cell, B-cell, antibody, complement, natural killer (NK) cell, macrophage, and inflammatory responses. Contemporary immunopharmacological strategies therefore increasingly combine costimulation blockade with complement inhibition, lymphocyte-directed therapy, and selected cytokine- or innate-immune interventions, with future regimens requiring closer integration of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic monitoring with donor genotype and organ-specific risk. Organoids and microfluidic vascular systems may provide an intermediate testing layer by quantifying antibody binding, complement activation, endothelial injury, coagulation, leukocyte transmigration, cytokine responses, and tissue-specific function under controlled conditions before escalation to large-animal studies. Artificial intelligence may further support xenoantigen discovery, genome-editing design, donor-recipient matching, multimodal rejection surveillance, and ultimately clinician-supervised immunopharmacological decision support. We propose that these components should be connected through a traceable design-build-test-learn workflow linking computational prediction, donor construction, standardized functional testing, non-human-primate validation, and early human data. Durable translation will depend not on any single technological advance, but on reproducible donor manufacturing, precision immune control, validated human-relevant test systems, standardized longitudinal data, pathogen surveillance, organ-specific management, and transparent regulatory governance.

papers.title: Elevated DSG3 Expression Is Correlated With Lung Cancer Progression and Poor Prognosis.
papers.authors: Yang J, Chen H, Hong J, Wang X.
papers.abstract: Desmoglein 3 (DSG3) is a member of the 7 transmembrane desmosomal cadherins and has been linked to pan-cancer onset and progression. However, its potential association with lung cancer remains unclear. DSG3 expression in lung cancer was evaluated in GEO and TCGA data. Furthermore, bioinformatics analysis was carried out to evaluate the association between immune infiltration and DSG3 expression, together with the clinical significance of DSG3 in lung cancer. GO, KEGG and GSEA enrichment analyses were conducted to dissect downstream signaling pathways associated with DSG3 dysregulation. In vitro functional experiments including CCK-8, colony formation, Transwell migration/invasion and western blot assays were carried out in A549 and H1299 cells with stable DSG3 knockdown to verify its oncogenic function and regulatory role in epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The data revealed that DSG3 was substantially upregulated in lung cancer and was linked with poorer clinicopathological characteristics and patients' prognosis. Moreover, DSG3 expression was markedly linked with immune cell infiltration in lung cancer. GSEA results further identified significant enrichment of keratinization, cornified envelope formation, matrisome remodeling, developmental biology and post-translational modification pathways in DSG3-high lung cancer samples. Cellular functional assays demonstrated that DSG3 silencing markedly suppressed the proliferation, migration and invasion of cells. Mechanistically, DSG3 knockdown upregulated epithelial marker E-cadherin while downregulating mesenchymal markers N-cadherin, Vimentin and EMT transcription factor Snail. This study showed that elevated DSG3 expression was linked with lung cancer progression and poor prognosis, while DSG3 downregulation inhibited lung cancer cells' migration, proliferation, and invasion by modulating EMT, highlighting DSG3's potential as a therapeutic, diagnostic, and prognostic target for lung cancer.

papers.title: The 32nd Annual Prostate Cancer Foundation Scientific Retreat Report.
papers.authors: Miyahira AK, Koo PJ.
papers.abstract: Background The 32nd Annual Prostate Cancer Foundation (PCF) Scientific Retreat took place in Carlsbad, CA on October 23-25, 2025. Methods The Annual PCF Scientific Retreat is a global forum for presenting the newest basic, translational, and clinical discoveries in prostate cancer, alongside work from related fields. Presentations highlight discoveries with strong potential to advance prostate cancer understanding, change clinical practice, and improve patient outcomes. Results The 2025 PCF Retreat featured research and special lectures from many disciplines, including: (i) next-generation theranostics; (ii) emerging immunotherapy approaches in prostate cancer; (iii) understanding and drugging the epigenome; (iv) clinical trial updates; (v) artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning; (vi) circulating biomarkers; (vii) harnessing the host microbiome in cancer; (viii) exercise interventions for patients with prostate cancer; (ix) CYP17A1-independent androgen biosynthesis as a mechanism of persistent androgen production; (x) Prostate Cancer Working Group 4 recommendations for trial design and response assessment; (xi) tissue-guided optimization of combination therapy; (xii) PCF Women in Science Lifetime Achievement Award lecture; and (xiii) bridging biomedical research and drug development. Conclusions The 2025 PCF Scientific Retreat illustrated how advances across diverse fields, including theranostics, immunotherapy, epigenetics, AI, and liquid biopsy, are converging to reshape how prostate cancer is understood, monitored, and treated. Recurring themes included tumor heterogeneity and lineage plasticity as determinants of treatment response, the need for predictive biomarkers to guide increasingly intensive and combination therapies, and the movement of effective therapies into earlier disease settings. This report reflects the state of the science as of October 2025.

papers.title: Intrinsically disordered ligands for the control of receptor uptake by endocytosis.
papers.authors: Park S, Sarro I, Nguyen T, Kamatar A, Wang L, Lafer EM, Rangamani P, Stachowiak JC.
papers.abstract: Endocytosis plays a crucial role in signaling, recycling, and degradation of receptors. Controlling endocytosis of specific receptors is therefore a major goal for both basic science and medicine. While antibody-induced dimerization can drive signaling-induced uptake of some receptors, the steric bulk of antibodies generally inhibits endocytosis, such that control over receptor uptake remains an unmet need. Recent work has demonstrated that attractive interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins drive inward membrane curvature, a key step in endocytosis. To harness this phenomenon for the control of receptor uptake, we designed chimeras that consisted of disordered domains fused to ligands for specific receptors. These chimeras condensed on membrane surfaces, in agreement with computational modeling, driving receptor clustering and uptake via clathrin-mediated endocytosis. In contrast, chimeras that repelled one another resisted condensation, helping receptors escape endocytosis and remain on the cell surface. Taken together, these results suggest that by modulating the amino acid sequence of intrinsically disordered ligands, we can promote or hinder the internalization of specific receptors by endocytic pathways. More broadly, these findings suggest a generalizable strategy for controlling the plasma membrane lifetime of diverse receptors, opening up new pathways for modulating cellular behavior and delivering therapeutics.
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: OR2B6 as a Prognostic Biomarker and Candidate Immunotherapeutic Target in Lung Adenocarcinoma: An Integrative Genomic and Transcriptomic Analysis.
papers.authors: Ba Y, Liu Y, Lv H, Li H, Zhu J, Zheng Y, Xing W.
papers.abstract: Introduction Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a common and aggressive subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, with a 5-year survival rate of less than 25%. Reliable biomarkers for prognosis and treatment remain urgently needed. This work explores the potential of OR2B6 as a prognostic biomarker and its relationship to immune infiltration in LUAD. Methods RNAseq data of 539 LUAD and 59 normal tissues were obtained from TCGA. Differential expression, diagnostic value, prognosis, regulatory networks, immune infiltration, TMB, MSI, and drug sensitivity correlations of OR2B6 were analysed using various R packages and bioinformatics tools. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis was performed using TISCH2. Somatic mutation profiles of OR2B6 expression were examined. qRT-PCR was used to confirm OR2B6 expression in LUAD tissues and cell lines. Results OR2B6 expression was significantly elevated in LUAD tissues compared to normal tissue (p Discussion OR2B6 is suggested to be a prognostic marker for LUAD. The observed association with immune infiltrations and immune checkpoint genes suggests that tumor immune evasion could be involved. The correlation with TMB and MSI further supports a potential role in immune response modulation. These findings provide a foundational basis for future research on OR2B6's role in LUAD and its potential as a candidate therapeutic target. As this is an exploratory analysis of public data, no a priori power calculation was performed, and the findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating pending validation in independent, adequately powered cohorts. Limitations include the use of public data and the need for functional validation. Conclusion OR2B6 represents a promising prognostic biomarker and candidate immunotherapy target in LUAD, with a promising association with clinical outcomes, immune infiltration, and drug sensitivity. However, these findings are correlative, and further functional and mechanistic studies are required to validate its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: In Silico Characterization of CXCL13+ Exhausted CD8+ T Cells in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Wang L, Guo S, Lu D.
papers.abstract: Background As a leading cause of cancer mortality, non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a major clinical challenge. Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy is an established treatment strategy for NSCLC, but the cellular and molecular features associated with this treatment context remain to be comprehensively explored. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE229353) from five NSCLC patients receiving pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy and one receiving chemotherapy alone were analyzed. After quality filtering, SCTransform normalization, PCA, Harmony integration, and unsupervised clustering, Cytotoxic T cells were further subclustered. Cell-cell communication, pseudotime trajectory, sample-level pseudobulk differential expression and Hallmark GSEA, transcription factor activity, and in silico CXCL13 perturbation analyses were performed. Results Ten major cell types and five Cytotoxic T cell subclusters were identified, including a CXCL13+ exhausted CD8+ T cell population enriched in T cell receptor and PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint-related pathways. CellChat revealed extensive predicted interactions with immune and stromal populations. Pseudotime analysis placed this population in intermediate-to-late regions of a continuous transcriptional trajectory. Sample-level pseudobulk analysis of the CXCL13+ exhausted CD8+ T cell subset showed exploratory enrichments of TNF/NF-κB and MYC-associated programs in the PD-1 + Chemo group and stronger interferon-response signatures in the Chemo group. The archived VIPER activity differences were summarized descriptively without significance claims. CXCL13 perturbation was associated with predicted changes in immune-related and metabolic pathways. Discussion The CXCL13+ exhausted CD8+ T cell population was observed in both treatment groups in NSCLC, exhibiting immune checkpoint enrichment, dynamic transcriptional states, predicted intercellular communication, and exploratory treatment-context- associated transcriptional differences. Computational perturbation analysis further suggested network-level associations involving CXCL13. These findings provide a cellular and molecular framework for further investigation, although validation in larger cohorts and experimental models remains necessary. Conclusion These findings characterize a CXCL13+ exhausted CD8+ T cell state observed in both treatment groups and provide hypotheses for further investigation. Given the small and highly unbalanced sample size and the computational nature of the analyses, independent cohort and experimental validation are required.

papers.title: Periplogenin rewires cholesterol-dependent signaling and antitumor immunity by targeting PCSK9 in cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Fu X, Pan Y, Wang X, Tao Y, Zhao R, Wei J, Ma Y, Yang M, Wang Y, Wang Q, Zhu Y, Xu L, Ren W, Wang Z, Wang L.
papers.abstract: Background Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is an aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options, underscoring the need to identify novel therapeutic agents and actionable molecular targets. Purpose This study aimed to identify natural compounds with antitumor activity against CCA and to elucidate their molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential. Study design A phenotype-based natural-product screening strategy was combined with mechanistic, genetic, multi-omics, and in vivo validation to identify and characterize periplogenin (PPG) as a candidate therapeutic agent for CCA. Methods The antitumor effects of PPG were evaluated using CCA cells, organoids, xenograft models, orthotopic tumor models, and immunocompetent CCA models. Integrative proteomic analyses were performed to identify PPG-regulated pathways. Molecular docking, Cellular Thermal Shift Assay (CETSA) and Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability (DARTS) assays were used to determine the direct molecular target of PPG, followed by PCSK9 knockout and methyl-β-cyclodextrin (MβCD) to assess target dependency and downstream mechanisms. Single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to characterize PPG-induced remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment, and the therapeutic efficacy of PPG combined with anti-PD-L1 treatment was further evaluated in vivo. Results PPG significantly suppressed CCA organoid outgrowth and metastatic potential, restrained tumorigenesis, and prolonged survival in orthotopic and xenograft CCA models. Integrative proteomics identified cholesterol metabolism and PI3K-AKT signaling as major pathways altered by PPG. PPG directly bound proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) and reduced PCSK9 abundance by promoting lysosomal degradation. Functionally, PPG increased cellular cholesterol and remodeled cholesterol-dependent membrane microdomains (lipid rafts), thereby attenuating PI3K-AKT activation. Cholesterol depletion with methyl-β-cyclodextrin blunted these effects. Genetic ablation of PCSK9 largely occluded PPG-induced cholesterol-lipid raft remodeling and diminished its antitumor efficacy, supporting PCSK9 dependence. Single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed that PPG increased cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell infiltration while reducing exhausted CD8+ T cells. Moreover, PPG potentiated anti-PD-L1 therapy and achieved superior tumor control in immunocompetent CCA models. Conclusion PPG exerts potent antitumor activity in CCA by directly targeting PCSK9 and inducing PCSK9-dependent cholesterol-membrane remodeling, which suppresses oncogenic PI3K-AKT signaling and enhances antitumor immunity. These findings identify PCSK9 as a druggable target of PPG and support PPG as a potential therapeutic strategy for CCA, particularly in combination with immune checkpoint blockade.
papers.venue: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology

papers.title: Single-cell and spatially resolved immune profiling in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a bibliometric and thematic analysis.
papers.authors: Li Y, Wang B, Zhang N, Peng G.
papers.abstract: Background Single-cell and spatially resolved technologies have expanded research on immune heterogeneity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We examined relationships among research themes, their cited foundations, and their temporal representation. Methods Web of Science Core Collection and PubMed were searched for publications dated from 1900 through July 1, 2026. After deduplication and screening, 587 English-language articles and reviews were included. Bibliometric networks were analyzed using VOSviewer, R, and bibliometrix. Document-level cosine overlaps between keyword and reference clusters were evaluated using stratified permutations with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Temporal analyses used keyword proportions and citation-weighted reference-year profiles within three descriptive windows. Sensitivity analyses examined database composition, inclusion thresholds, and individual recent references. Results Publication output increased after 2021. China had the largest publication output, while the United States had the highest citation count and international-collaboration total link strength. Co-citation and keyword analyses identified four and three domains, respectively. K3-C2 had the largest observed cosine score (0.661), exceeding its null mean by 0.039 (adjusted P = 0.0072); K1-C1 also exceeded its null expectation (adjusted P = 0.0012). Among keyword-available publications, spatial transcriptomics increased from 0.0% to 1.7% and 8.3% across the three windows. The recent reference subset contained five references, all published in 2024; its C2 share was sensitive to individual references. Keyword-cluster agreement was high across database sources and moderate at the stricter occurrence threshold. Conclusion The analysis identifies relationships among immune, cellular, stromal, spatial, and computational literature domains and descriptive changes in keyword representation. These findings provide a quantitative literature framework for further investigation of HNSCC immune profiling.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial omics in urologic cancer immunotherapy: bibliometric and registry mapping with an exploratory full-text assessment.
papers.authors: Zhou D, Li J, Tang C, Wang Y, Song C.
papers.abstract: Background Single-cell and spatial omics can inform research on immunotherapy response and resistance. We mapped publication activity and ClinicalTrials.gov study designs and explored evidence types in a targeted full-text subset of urologic cancer studies. Methods Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus records published in 2008-2025 were locked on 13 July 2026. Revision-stage eligibility reconciliation retained 538 records; 466 native Web of Science records supplied temporal-analysis inputs. A targeted full-text assessment was supplemented by a random audit of 100 previously non-selected records and independent reassessment of 40 selected studies. Evidence classes included treatment-exposed human data, association replication, computational proxies, experimental mechanisms, and prognosis. ClinicalTrials.gov records were analyzed separately. Results The 538-record corpus included 440 publications from 2023-2025 (81.8%). The targeted assessment included 122 original studies among 135 assessed reports. In the random audit, 15/100 records were C1 or C2b: three C1 and 12 C2b. One C1 report contained cell-level descriptive evidence without a patient-level marker-outcome analysis. The initial evidence-class agreement was 92/100 (Cohen's kappa, 0.890) in this audit and 31/40 (kappa, 0.682) in the selected-study reassessment. Public-cohort reuse and exploratory analyses limited clinical interpretation. Of 10 ClinicalTrials.gov records, one had a verified reported omics component, eight documented planned or ongoing components, and one was withdrawn without accrual. Conclusion Bibliometric activity increased in the retained corpus. The random audit identified treatment-related reports missed by targeted retrieval, limiting claims about evidence completeness. Cell-level descriptions, patient-level associations, and locked-model validation require separate interpretation. Neither selected-study proportions nor bibliometric attention establishes field-wide clinical maturity. Registry plans require component-specific verification of implementation and reporting.

papers.title: Dynamics of Drosophila immune stress hematopoiesis assessed by single cell transcriptomics.
papers.authors: Morin-Poulard I, Liu X, Tian Y, Montemurro M, Sheng L, Labourdette D, Vanzo N, Crozatier M.
papers.abstract: The molecular complexity of the hematopoietic microenvironment (niche) and its response to immune stress remain largely unknown. Here, we establish the transcriptional profile of the lymph gland, the Drosophila hematopoietic organ, and its associated niche, the posterior signaling center, at single-cell resolution and at different time points following an immune challenge. Among blood cells, we identify permanent cellular states present with and without stress, but also transient states specific to the immune response, which correspond to dividing cells primed to differentiate into dedicated effector cells. The niche itself is a heterogeneous cell population, and most niche cells undergo dynamic transcriptional remodeling following immune stress. Finally, we identify two new players involved in the hematopoietic stress response: the immune deficiency pathway and the cholecystokinin-like receptor, both of which are expressed in niche cell subsets during immune stress conditions. This molecular atlas of lymph gland cells at different time points after an immune challenge provides new insights into the control of stress hematopoiesis by discrete niche cell subsets.

papers.title: Controversies and consensus on immune function and long-term health risks following adult thymectomy: a comprehensive review of molecular mechanisms and real-world evidence.
papers.authors: Zhao P, Li X, Wang X, Xu T, Lu H.
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate the long-term immunological, oncological, and clinical consequences of adult thymectomy by synthesizing recent basic, translational, and real-world clinical evidence. Background Historical surgical paradigms regarded the post-pubertal adult thymus as an immunologically redundant, fatty involuted organ, justifying routine "incidental" resection during cardiac procedures. A high-profile 2023 cohort study in The New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM) challenged this concept, reporting that adult thymectomy significantly increased 5-year all-cause mortality and cancer risk. Subsequent population-level studies (US SEER/NCDB, French PMSI) and deep-learning imaging cohorts have sparked debate, offering both corroborating and conflicting insights into adult thymic function. Methods and synthesis This review synthesizes cellular mechanisms (TREC dynamics, TCR repertoire contraction, senescence-associated T cells, Treg lineage stability) and endocrine factors (thymulin-mediated myeloid regulation) with clinical data stratified by age at surgery, indication, resection extent, and follow-up duration. Conclusions The adult thymus remains functionally active, exporting naïve T cells and humoral immunomodulators like thymulin that maintain peripheral immune tolerance and restrain inflammaging. Clinical evaluation must differentiate between incidental resection (which induces avoidable iatrogenic immunosenescence) and therapeutic resection (e.g., for thymic epithelial tumors or myasthenia gravis), where removing a diseased, immunosuppressive microenvironment can reduce secondary cancer risk. Partial thymectomy (PT) is emerging as an option to preserve immunocompetence when oncologically feasible.

papers.title: T/NK-cell remodeling and IFN-responsive myeloid activation delineate immunometabolic risk profiles in chronic active Epstein-Barr virus disease.
papers.authors: Cao Y, Zhou Z, Yu S, Liang Y, Zhao C, Li X, Zhang Z, Zheng J, Ruan Q, Gao Y, Yang Q, Shao L, Zhang W.
papers.abstract: Background Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus disease (CAEBV) is a rare EBV-associated T/NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by persistent viral infection, systemic inflammation, and highly variable clinical courses. Patients may develop HLH-like hyperinflammation, severe organ involvement, lymphoma transformation, or death, yet current assessment does not fully explain why patients with similar viral burden follow divergent trajectories. Methods We integrated PBMC single-cell RNA-sequencing profiles from healthy controls and CAEBV samples with a retrospective cohort of 130 independent CAEBV patients to connect cellular immune remodeling with clinically measurable features. Results Single-cell analysis identified T/NK remodeling toward cytotoxic, exhaustion-associated, senescence-associated, and metabolically altered states, accompanied by IFN-responsive, antigen-presenting myeloid programs. Ligand-receptor and receiver-side analyses prioritized candidate IFNγ-associated T/NK-to-myeloid communication within this IFN-responsive program, linking NK and CD8+ T-cell states with myeloid inflammatory activation. Guided by these findings, we mapped inflammatory, metabolic, coagulation, and lymphocyte-subset variables into a biology-informed clinical immunometabolic index reflecting inflammatory cytokine activation, metabolic stress, and adaptive immune contraction. Internally defined index strata were associated with increasing CAEBV+HLH, death, and severe-disease burden. Unsupervised clinical mapping further identified three exploratory but interpretable immunometabolic patterns, including immune-metabolically preserved, intermediate immune-contraction, and IFNγ-high immunometabolic high-risk, with distinct immune-cell, inflammatory, metabolic, and outcome profiles. Conclusions Together, these findings organize CAEBV heterogeneity around linked T/NK remodeling, myeloid activation, and systemic immunometabolic stress. This single-cell-informed clinical-pattern map complements EBV-DNA and organ-size assessment and supports prospective validation of clinically measurable, mechanism-guided monitoring and intervention strategies.

papers.title: The spatial immune geography of resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: ecosystem architecture of perioperative immunotherapy response and relapse.
papers.authors: Qi S, Zhou X, Liu C, Zhou Q.
papers.abstract: Perioperative immune-checkpoint blockade has improved pathological and event-free outcomes in resectable non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but benefit remains heterogeneous and current biomarkers do not reliably distinguish tumor eradication from transient control or future relapse. This limitation partly reflects how tumors are measured: programed death ligand 1 expression, tumor mutational burden and bulk immune-cell abundance compress a spatially organized ecosystem into summary values. Here, we define the spatial immune geography of resectable NSCLC across four coupled scales: intratumor territories, cellular neighborhoods, regional immune structures-including tertiary lymphoid structures and tumor-draining lymph nodes-and longitudinal transitions from pretreatment biopsy to resection, molecular residual disease and recurrence. We critically synthesize human evidence linking T-cell access, antigen-presentation circuits, B-cell and tertiary-lymphoid organization, and stromal, myeloid and hypoxic niches to perioperative immunotherapy response. We further distinguish pretreatment predictors from treatment-induced pharmacodynamic changes and explain why pathological response and biological cure are related but non-equivalent endpoints. On this basis, we propose a testable spatial-immune-resilience framework comprising eradication-permissive, persistence-prone and escape-permissive ecosystems. We also evaluate how multiplex imaging, spatial transcriptomics, digital spatial profiling, anatomically registered single-cell analysis and computational pathology differ in biological reach and translational readiness. Finally, we outline an assay-to-decision validation pathway that integrates standardized multiregion tissue sampling, tumor-draining lymph nodes and circulating tumor DNA. Spatial profiling is unlikely to transform perioperative care through maximal molecular resolution alone; its clinical value will depend on reproducible, parsimonious measurements that improve decisions beyond stage, pathology and molecular residual disease.

papers.title: Cell-informed host-response profiling distinguishes neutrophil-like and PLA2G7-associated immunometabolic axes in systemic infection.
papers.authors: Gu Y, Yu Y, Zhang W, Liu W, Zhao C, Ding S.
papers.abstract: Background Whole-blood host-response signatures can distinguish infection-positive from infection-negative systemic inflammation, but their signal combines changes in leucocyte composition with regulation within cells. We asked whether a retrospectively selected and subsequently fixed blood transcriptomic framework could relate candidate transcripts to granulocyte-associated and monocyte/macrophage-associated expression contexts rather than serve as another stand-alone diagnostic product.
