Methods A 12-gene framework was retrospectively derived from four contrasts across three studies (444 contrast-level observations; 443 unique arrays) and subsequently fixed for external evaluation using a single-sample transcriptome-rank score. Performance was examined separately across cohorts with different specimens, age groups and comparators. Transcript-score sensitivity analyses, donor-level whole-blood single-cell pseudobulk and cell-line qRT-PCR were used to assess candidate localization and cell-line expression-context concordance. Cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation and colocalisation were included as exploratory genetic context. Results In the closest target-context cohort, GSE134347, the fixed score achieved an AUROC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.764-0.889) for sepsis versus non-infectious critical illness. Performance was lower in pediatric day-1 SIRS comparisons, indicating dependence on population and comparator context. Adjustment for alternative neutrophil-associated transcript scores produced a marker-dependent ordering, with SMPDL3A among the most attenuated and PLA2G7 among the least attenuated candidates; no candidate remained FDR-significant in the primary six-gene family. Donor-level single-cell analysis and qRT-PCR supported a monocyte/macrophage context for PLA2G7 and granulocyte-like localization of the diagnostic immune markers. Exploratory Mendelian randomisation did not support a susceptibility effect for the testable immunometabolism-associated candidates, and the HLA-DRB1 regional signal lacked evidence of a shared variant under single-variant colocalisation assumptions. Conclusion This study provides an auditable, cell-informed framework that relates granulocyte-associated transcription to PLA2G7-associated monocyte/macrophage localization within the whole-blood infection response. The framework is intended for biological prioritisation, and it defines testable candidates for future studies.

papers.title: Deep learning-based integrative single-cell transcriptomic analysis of vitiligo.
papers.authors: Xiang F, Ding Y, Zhang J, Yu S, Zhang X, Wang H, Qiu Y, Yin H, Kang X.
papers.abstract: Introduction Vitiligo is an immune-mediated depigmentation disorder in which interferon-γ signalling and autoreactive CD8+ T cells are central, but the cross-cohort cellular ecosystem and donor-level disease signature remain incompletely resolved. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of three public skin single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets comprising 35 donors and 93,287 post-quality-control cells. We combined donor-aware cell-composition and pseudobulk analyses with a deep attention multiple-instance learning model, and reserved a separate balanced patient -control cohort for independent evaluation. Results Eleven major cell populations were identified. The donor-level classifier achieved 0.914 accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.990 in donor-stratified five-fold cross-validation. After Benjamini -Hochberg correction across 11 cell types, vitiligo lesions showed macrophage expansion and depletion of fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and mast cells (all q = 0.029). Integrated ranking prioritised an interferon-γ/CXCL9 -CXCL10 programme, while CD8+ T cells displayed Trm-associated and cytotoxic-effector transcriptional states. An eight-feature signature trained only in the primary discovery cohort achieved an area under the curve of 0.944 (95% CI, 0.778 -1.000) and accuracy of 0.750 (95% CI, 0.468 -0.911) in a small independent cohort of six healthy controls and six patients with vitiligo; exact label permutation supported discrimination ( p = 0.003). A directional omnibus test across ten prespecified validation measures supported panel-level concordance ( p = 0.023), although no individual measure remained significant after multiple-testing correction. Discussion These findings provide preliminary external support for a multivariable signal connecting an expanded macrophage compartment, interferon-associated chemokine signalling, and Trm-like CD8+ T-cell states.

papers.title: Qingjin Desheng Pian attenuates NSCLC progression by suppressing neutrophil extracellular trap formation: involvement of the HMGB1/TLR2/MyD88 axis.
papers.authors: Qin B, Huang S, Ma C, Zhou R, Zhou D, Tang Y.
papers.abstract: Background Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Despite advances in immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy, a substantial proportion of patients derive limited benefit. In the tumor microenvironment, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) promote tumor progression and metastasis, representing a potential therapeutic target. Qingjin Desheng Pian (QJDS) is a standardized hospital preparation of traditional Chinese medicine that has been used clinically for primary and metastatic lung cancer. Although earlier studies have suggested antitumor effects of QJDS, its impact on NET formation and the underlying mechanisms in NSCLC remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether QJDS suppresses NET formation and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms. Methods This retrospective study included 209 stage III-IV NSCLC patients who received QJDS plus chemotherapy or chemotherapy alone. NET enrichment was assessed by single-cell RNA sequencing and histopathology. Network pharmacology predicted potential targets. A syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma model evaluated antitumor efficacy and intratumoral NET levels. In vitro , primary mouse neutrophils were stimulated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) for NET induction, followed by QJDS intervention. Transcriptomic sequencing and weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified hub genes. Pharmacological rescue experiments using N4-acetylcytidine (N4A) were performed. Results QJDS prolonged progression-free survival, improved quality of life, and attenuated systemic inflammation. NETs were markedly enriched in NSCLC tumor tissues compared with adjacent tissues. QJDS dose-dependently inhibited tumor growth and reduced intratumoral NET formation and serum MPO-DNA levels in vivo . In vitro , QJDS suppressed NET release and attenuated NET-mediated migration, invasion, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and proliferation of lung cancer cells. Mechanistically, high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) was identified as a key hub gene through transcriptomic and weighted gene co-expression network analyses. QJDS significantly downregulated HMGB1, toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2), and myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88) expression in neutrophils, effects partially reversed by N4A. Conclusion These findings indicate that QJDS attenuates NSCLC progression by suppressing NET formation through mechanisms involving the HMGB1/TLR2/MyD88 axis, supporting its adjuvant application in advanced lung cancer.

papers.title: Early Brucella abortus infection reshapes the exosomal lncRNA cargo of macrophages and highlights putative immunoregulatory pathways.
papers.authors: Álvarez F, Gutiérrez E, Ferrari Í, Arriagada V, Ruiz S, Díaz B, Gómez LA, Oñate ÁA.
papers.abstract: Brucella abortus is an intracellular pathogen that profoundly alters macrophage responses, but the contribution and extracellular distribution of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) during infection remain poorly characterized. Here, we characterized the exosomal lncRNA landscape of B. abortus -infected RAW 264.7 macrophages and applied an integrated bioinformatic framework to prioritize candidate lncRNAs and their potential functional contexts. Exosomes were isolated from infected and control macrophages at 8 h post-infection, and their RNA content was analyzed by high-throughput sequencing. Differential expression analysis identified 83 lncRNAs with altered expression, with most showing reduced expression in exosomes from infected cells. Functional enrichment analysis of protein-coding genes located within ±250 kb of the differentially expressed lncRNAs generated associations with immune-related processes, including antigen presentation and cytotoxicity, as well as ion transport, lipid metabolism, and lymphocyte-related processes. A complementary Enrichr analysis provided complementary immune-related signals, although these did not remain significant after multiple-testing corrections. Malat1 , Neat1 , and Gas5 were selected for RT-qPCR validation and showed expression patterns consistent with sequencing. AlphaFold 3 predicted Snu13 as a potential interactor of the three candidate lncRNAs, providing a hypothesis for future experimental investigation but not establishing a role in exosomal RNA sorting. Overall, these findings provide a transcriptomic resource and computational framework for prioritizing exosomal lncRNAs associated with B. abortus infection and support further investigation of EV-associated lncRNA loading mechanism and their potential functional relevance.

papers.title: Inter-organ interaction axes in systemic inflammation: network pathological mechanisms, pharmacological targets, and precision treatment strategies.
papers.authors: Xie S, Tian H, Song Y, Liang F.
papers.abstract: Systemic inflammation plays a central role in both acute and chronic pathological states. Acute inflammation is often triggered by infections or trauma, characterized by rapid immune activation low-grade inflammation is closely associated with aging-related diseases such as cardiovascular diseases and diabetes. During disease progression, inter-organ communication forms dynamic networks mediated by metabolites, immune factors, and neural signals, further amplifying the inflammatory response. This article focuses on three key inter-organ interaction axes: the gut-liver-brain axis, the adipose-muscle-bone axis, and the heart-kidney-lung axis. It discusses microbiota-driven metabolic neuroinflammation, immune-metabolic imbalance-induced tissue remodeling, and endothelial and microcirculatory damage in the context of multi-organ inflammation. Based on axis-specific molecular targets and spatiotemporal precision, pharmacological strategies are shifting from single-factor interventions to multitarget combination therapies. Meanwhile, innovative technologies such as single-cell multi-omics, spatial omics, artificial intelligence (AI), and organ-on-a-chip are expediting precision medicine approaches for the individualized treatment of systemic inflammation.

papers.title: Transcriptomic identification of mitophagy-related plaque markers HAND2 , NRP1 and RNF213 , with external replication and in vivo validation of MLXIP .
papers.authors: Wang D, He X, Lian S, Fu Y, Liang C, Wang J, Liu X.
papers.abstract: Background Atherosclerosis is a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, and mitophagy dysfunction contributes to its pathogenesis. However, the mitophagy-related molecular signatures that could serve as plaque-associated markers remain incompletely characterized. Methods Paired differential expression analysis of GSE43292 (32 plaque vs. 32 paired macroscopically intact carotid samples), combined with weighted gene co-expression network analysis, defined a plaque-associated module that was intersected with 4,922 mitophagy-associated genes (GeneCards) to identify mitophagy-related DEGs. LASSO, Random Forest and XGBoost were applied as an auxiliary, patient-grouped, cross-validated feature-selection step; a logistic-regression model fitted on the shared genes was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). External validation used GSE100927 (69 plaque vs. 35 control peripheral artery samples). Immune infiltration was assessed by CIBERSORT, and MLXIP protein abundance was explored by Western blot in a small ApoE ⁻/⁻ murine model. Comparator specimens were macroscopically intact tissue (Stary types I-II). Results Paired analysis of GSE43292 identified 1,249 differentially expressed genes, of which 107 were mitophagy-related. Patient-grouped machine-learning feature selection nominated three consensus markers- HAND2 , NRP1 and RNF213 -and a three-gene logistic-regression model reached an out-of-fold area under the curve (AUC) of 0.892 (95% CI 0.810-0.973); because selection and evaluation used the same cohort, these results are exploratory. All three were directionally reproduced in the independent external cohort GSE100927 (direction-locked AUC 0.814, 0.942 and 0.848 respectively). Of three genes examined a priori , MLXIP and EPB41L4A-AS1 replicated in the external cohort (AUC 0.834 for both), whereas RNU4ATAC did not (AUC 0.321). CIBERSORT showed higher macrophage and memory B-cell fractions and lower regulatory T-cell fractions in plaques. In an exploratory in vivo experiment ( n = 3 per group), aortic MLXIP protein was 37.7-fold higher in atherosclerotic mice than in controls ( P = 0.11) with unchanged MLXIP mRNA; these data were directional only. Conclusion In this exploratory study, bioinformatics and machine learning nominated HAND2 , NRP1 and RNF213 as candidate mitophagy-related plaque markers, with MLXIP and EPB41L4A-AS1 replicated in an independent cohort, and pointed to a mitophagy-immune axis in plaque pathogenesis. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis following CRISPR/Cas9 knockdown demonstrates a novel role for human T cell-intrinsic IL-1β in determining T cell metabolic landscape.
papers.authors: Kale K, Vemulawada C, Rogers KJ, Crawford MP, Heath J, Karandikar NJ.
papers.abstract: T helper 17 (Th17) CD4+ T cells are key mediators of autoimmune pathology. Interleukin (IL)-1β is a potent proinflammatory cytokine known to promote Th17 differentiation and pathogenicity, in combination with other cytokines. Whereas recent studies have shown that T cells are capable of expressing IL-1β themselves, the role of this T cell-endogenous IL-1β is poorly understood. Using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of IL1B in naïve human CD4+ T cells along with cytokine neutralization and IL-1 receptor blockade, we found that T cell-intrinsic IL-1β is not essential for Th17 differentiation or effector resistance. Remarkably, single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that IL1B deletion profoundly rewires the transcriptional and metabolic landscape within the T cells, suppressing glycolytic and hypoxia-responsive pathways. These findings uncouple T cell-intrinsic IL-1β from Th17 effector resistance while uncovering an important contribution toward sustaining metabolic roles. This refines our understanding of IL-1β biology and informs therapeutic strategies in immune-mediated disease settings.

papers.title: Cross-Species Single-Cell, Single-Nucleus, and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal Remodeling Features of the Immune Microenvironment and Tissue Architecture Associated With Prostate Aging and Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
papers.authors: Li Z, Luo Y, Zhu S, Yu B, Li K, Dai X, Tan S, Su H, Chen W, Deng Y, Yuan D, Du A, Jia Z, Jiang K, Yang Y, Zhu J.
papers.abstract: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is closely associated with advancing age, but the tissue, cellular, and molecular features associated with prostate aging and BPH remain incompletely understood. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from Homo sapiens (Hsa) and Mus musculus (Mmu), single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data from Macaca fascicularis (Mfa), and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data from Hsa to characterize prostate remodeling across the available age groups. Cross-species integration using one-to-one ortholog mapping and scGen-based batch correction generated a prostate atlas comprising 47 samples and more than 400,000 cells. In species-specific analyses, CD4_Tem, CD4_Treg, CD8_CTL, Macro_IL1B, and Macro_LYVE1 were more abundant in Middle-aged or Old groups. These populations exhibited diverse pathway signatures related to inflammation, angiogenesis, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. In addition, basal, club, and hillock cells exhibited higher scores for EMT-related transcriptional features and features associated with ECM remodeling in Old Hsa and Old Mmu groups. Fibro_IL1R1, Fibro_C7, and SMC_CNN1 were more abundant in Old Hsa and Old Mmu groups, with higher activity of pathways related to inflammation and ECM remodeling. Tip endothelial cells were more abundant in Old Hsa and Old Mmu groups, with higher angiogenesis-related pathway activity, whereas venous endothelial cells had higher activity of pathways related to inflammation and ECM remodeling. In summary, our study characterizes remodeling features of the immune microenvironment and tissue architecture associated with prostate aging and BPH across species.

papers.title: Identification of Immune-Associated Hub Genes Related to the G2/M Checkpoint Pathway in Bladder Cancer Through Integrated Bioinformatics Analysis.
papers.authors: Kumari R, Bhushan A, Kaur J, Nagar PK, Wasson M, Agrawal U.
papers.abstract: Objectives Bladder cancer is a highly heterogeneous malignancy characterized by complex immune interactions that influence disease progression and patient outcomes. Identifying immune-related molecular determinants with prognostic and therapeutic relevance is therefore critical. This study aimed to systematically investigate immune-related genes involved in bladder cancer and to identify key predictive molecular prognostic biomarkers, with particular emphasis on cell-cycle-associated immune mechanisms. Methods RNA expression profiles from bladder tumor and corresponding normal tissues were analyzed across five independent cohorts (GSE13507, GSE19915, GSE40355, GSE42089, and TCGA-Bladder Cancer). Common differentially expressed immune-related genes (DEIRGs) were identified using GEO2R and TCGA analyses. Functional enrichment and pathway analyses were performed using Metascape and DAVID, while hub genes were identified through protein-protein interaction networks using MCODE, CytoHubba, and ClueGO. Expression patterns, prognostic relevance, and immune associations were validated using UALCAN, the Human Protein Atlas, TIMER2.0, and PrognoScan databases. Results A total of 300 common DEIRGs were identified across datasets. Network analysis revealed 21 significant immune-related hub genes, several of which were consistently enriched in the G2M checkpoint pathway. Eleven hub genes were significantly associated with reduced overall survival in bladder cancer patients. Notably, six G2M checkpoint-related genes ( TOP2A, CCNA2, CDK1, BIRC5, PLK1, and E2F1 ) demonstrated strong prognostic relevance across multiple cohorts. Conclusions This comprehensive in silico analysis highlights the critical role of G2M checkpoint-associated immune-related genes in bladder cancer progression. These genes represent predictive molecular prognostic immune biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets, providing a foundation for the development of personalized immunotherapeutic strategies in bladder cancer.

papers.title: Single-cell analysis identifies a proliferative osteoblastic subpopulation and machine learning-derived prognostic signatures in osteosarcoma.
papers.authors: Wang J, Luo Q, Xie P, Liu Y, Zhang H, Meng W, Deng T.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) shows marked cellular heterogeneity, and patients often have very different clinical outcomes despite similar clinicopathological features. This variability remains difficult to explain using conventional risk factors alone. Here, we combined single-cell transcriptomic analysis, bulk transcriptomic profiling and machine-learning modeling to identify prognostic signatures related to tumor proliferation and the immune microenvironment. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from GSE152048 (n = 11) were used to map the cellular composition of OS. Within the osteoblastic compartment, we identified a proliferative subpopulation enriched for chromosome segregation, mitotic division and microtubule-related processes. We then used the TCGA-SARC cohort (n = 261) for model development and the GSE39058 osteosarcoma cohort (n = 41) for external validation. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis, differential expression analysis and univariate Cox regression were used to screen genes associated with immune features, proliferative activity and prognosis. These genes were defined as immune-proliferation-related signatures (IPRS). Among 117 machine-learning models, the random survival forest model performed best overall, with a 10-fold cross-validated C-index of 0.755 in the TCGA training cohort, an external validation C-index of 0.782 in GSE39058 and an average C-index of 0.769. The IPRS score separated patients into distinct prognostic groups and remained independently associated with overall survival in multivariate Cox analysis. It was also related to immune and stromal scores, immune-cell infiltration patterns and predicted drug sensitivity. We further selected ALG6 for experimental validation. Knockdown of ALG6 reduced proliferation and colony formation and increased apoptosis in 143B and U2OS cells. Overall, these results support the prognostic relevance of IPRS in osteosarcoma and suggest that ALG6 warrants further mechanistic investigation.

papers.title: Case report: single-cell characterization of cerebrospinal fluid in a lung squamous cell carcinoma patient with brain metastasis.
papers.authors: Wu WT, Lu JJ, Chen S, Zhang YR, Du YY.
papers.abstract: Brain metastasis (BrM) originating from lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) confers a dismal prognosis due to limited therapeutic options and immunotherapy resistance. Here, we report a 70-year-old man with advanced LUSC and BrM who experienced intracranial progression during camrelizumab-based chemoimmunotherapy and subsequently received radiotherapy and modified chemotherapy, with an overall survival of five months. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of a cerebrospinal fluid sample, integrated with public primary and metastatic datasets, identified a CD8 + T-cell cluster enriched for a stress-response program. Exploratory analyses of public transcriptomic cohorts suggested an association between a higher stress response T-cell (Tstr) signature and unfavorable outcomes.

papers.title: Formulation of a Novel NS5A- and NS5B-Based Chimeric Vaccine Against Hepatitis C Virus: An Artificial Intelligence-Supported Approach.
papers.authors: Niknam M, Zohrabzadeh M, Hahashempour A, Honari Jahromi A, Nazari MK, Hajizade MS.
papers.abstract: Objectives We aimed to design a multiepitope vaccine against hepatitis C virus (HCV) with the potential to elicit broad protective immunity against diverse HCV genotypes through computational design. Method : One hundred sequences of the most widespread subtypes of HCV were retrieved from the Los Alamos National Laboratory database, and consensus sequences of the NS5A and NS5B proteins were generated to construct an efficient vaccine for human use. Numerous B-cell lymphocyte, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte and helper T-lymphocyte epitopes located in the conserved domains of HCV proteins and similar in human and mouse alleles were evaluated criteria for use in the vaccine construct. Results Population coverage analysis identified that substantial parts of the worldwide population carry epitopes and their corresponding alleles within their genome, which confirms that the vaccine candidate is an effective agent against this lethal disease. Codon optimization and in silico cloning of eukaryotic and prokaryotic vectors validated the strong expression of the vaccine construct in the host systems. Molecular docking analysis revealed favorable binding affinities between the vaccine construct and toll-like receptors, which confirmed the vaccine's capacity to induce robust and stable immune responses against the hepatitis C virus. Conclusion We incorporated new bioinformatic methods to design multiepitope vaccine against HCV. The development of a vaccine targeting multi genotypes of HCV could potentially provide for long-term protection against infection and may mitigate the risk of drug resistance across various genotypes and subtypes. Current research emphasizes the need for a vaccine that can elicit comprehensive immune responses, including both neutralizing antibodies and T-cell responses, to effectively address the genetic diversity of the virus. Future experimental studies are essential to validate predicted immunogenicity, structural stability, and protective efficacy before clinical consideration.
